The Only Jeans I’ve Bought In Almost 2 Years

By
Julieta
-
August 24, 2026
0
Share
Facebook
X
Pinterest
Linkedin
Email

    First pair of jeans in 20+ months?

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 4:36
    Instaread

    Don’t ask me why. Mental and physical energy to look for, order, try on and return when you haven’t had a full night since pregnancy? Most likely.

    Let’s attribute it to energy conservation, especially for me, a projector in human design.

    Because the truth is, one pair of Frame barrel jeans, two Joe’s Mia wide legs, and a pair of Rag and Bone sweatpant jeans I got during early postpartum have been in heavy rotation since I had my third baby over 20 months ago. Most of them are between 3-5 years old. And they’ve carried me through.

    Jeans (25 P) – same jeans different wash: these or these | similar wash + jeans l Boots

    I’m past big try-ons. And while I never accumulated much, it feels good to give a ton of wear to great pieces you invested in. Isn’t that what cost per wear is all about?

    But it’s also something deeper than that. It’s having such a good relationship with who you are and your style that these pieces can come with you through the shittiest rebirths and life evolutions.

    Jeans (25 P) – same jeans different wash: these or these | similar wash + jeans l Cardigan (S) l Similar Boots

    I believe your closet is a big puzzle reflecting all of the many pieces your identity contains. When it’s aligned, it can evolve with you. The pieces chosen from clarity don’t expire. They just keep showing up for you.

    My Most Worn Jeans Right Now: Pilcro Kayden Carpenter Barrel Jeans

    So these jeans (or these)? I’ll give initial thanks to Kat. She shared her new barrel jeans a while back, and while clicking to see hers, the Pilcro Kayden High Rise Carpenter Barrel Jeans popped up. I hit purchase on the spot.

    My exact pair is sold out, but these + these are the same style in different washes, and these are a similar wash + similar style (with the exact same name?? Just the pockets are different). And if you want something more fun, they come in so many colors, embroideries, and more.

    Jeans (25 P) – same jeans different wash: these or these | similar wash + jeans | similar wash + jeans

    They were exactly what my closet was asking for. A good pair of chic, dark wash jeans. I’ve always known dark washes style easier with my closet, and my favorite colors. The whole look feels so me.

    And this postpartum season I decided I needed interesting details in my jeans to make my new mom-of-three life more, well, interesting.

    These have it. So much so, they made me come out of my postpartum and business rebuilding bubble to talk about them.

    Sizing & Styling Details

    Jeans (25 P) – same jeans different wash: these or these | similar wash + jeans l Similar Boots

    • The fit is perfect for those of us who want to widen our hips a bit. In my case, breastfeeding is keeping a lot of my weight on top, so most times I feel my best when I create more volume in my lower body.
    • Depending on the look you feel best in, these can be perfect or too big in your true size. I decided to size down to avoid a more prominent and baggy barrel look that feels too overwhelming for me.
    • Length wise, I tried both the regular and petite, and decided on the petite because I mostly wear low heels. This length allows for both flat and low heeled shoes, helping me get more wear out of them. Truth be told I’ve considered getting them in regular for the few times I wear higher heels.
    • It’s often said dark washes are more for winter and lighter washes for summer, but I don’t believe in that. I love these with a lot of my summer tops, and the fabric is light so they don’t feel heavy for the weather.

    Energy preservation made me forget about bum pics, but the retailer pics are very close. These were the details on top of the dark wash that made me say yes.

    If they feel you, just as much as they felt very me, get them here.

    Besos,
    Julieta

    If you resonated with your closet being a big puzzle reflecting all of the many pieces your identity contains, and how choosing pieces with clarity can come with you through the shittiest evolutions, I’m creating something for you. Be the first to know here.
